column5: susie_twas cell -> fine_mapping.R (QtlFineMappingResult for test_study ENSG00000283047 over qtl_mini) run with --seed 1 (the notebook `seed` parameter is forwarded to fine_mapping.R). Bit-identical across two seeded reruns; no embedded absolute paths. The x86/ARM CI matrix may need a looser rtol (calibrate from the first CI run). Re-baselined for PR #1422 (SuSiE L default 10, greedy-L off): the fit now uses a FIXED 10 single effects where the greedy search previously settled on 5, so alpha goes 5xP -> 10xP and the diffuse PIP mass scales with L. The locus yields no credible sets either way, so no conclusion changes. Greedy-off is what makes this platform-stable: with greedy on the retained count was 5 on macOS and 10 on Linux, a shape difference no tolerance could absorb. Re-baselined again for pecotmr 0.9.0: the susie_twas cell now passes --cv-folds/--cv-threads to the fine-mapping pass as well, because a cross-validated fine-mapping-derived weight method (susie) needs each fold's own fine-mapping fit -- 0.9.0 aborts otherwise (.twasCheckFmCvPresent). The only delta is that cvResult is now populated (samplePartition/prediction/performance/foldFits) where it was NULL; everything else is identical at 1e-6. rtol LOOSENED 1e-6 -> 1e-5 after the first CI matrix run on this fixture (the note above anticipated it): with cvResult now populated, each CV fold's SuSiE prior variance V (~6e-4) differs by 1.02e-6 and 1.04e-6 relative on ubuntu-24.04-arm while matching exactly on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (actions run 38183809313). Re-baselined 2026-10-13: genomicRegion() is now the ANALYSIS WINDOW, stored at construction, rather than the derived span of the variants that survived QC -- the span is still available as range(x). The collection therefore carries a `region` mcols column and the per-row grange_start/grange_end are populated (previously NA on every path, because no caller passed `region` to postprocessFinemappingFits). Verified the ONLY change: with the `region` column and grange_* dropped, old vs new are all.equal at 1e-6. The cis/gene path, as for fine_mapping.ENSG00000283047.rds. Re-baselined 2026-10-15 for the pecotmr published-output rework (resultWriters.R: writeFineMappingBed/writeSumStatsVcf -> exportToBed/exportToVcf). Verified no existing value moved: over the columns both versions carry and that were populated before, old vs new are all.equal at 1e-6. Adds the dataSource / standardized / z_supplied provenance columns. Re-baselined 2026-10-16 against the installed pecotmr 0.9.3: `standardized` is FALSE -> TRUE. It is DERIVED, not declared -- .fmRecordProvenance() reads .qtlScaleResiduals(), and residualizedGenotypes() scales each genotype column to unit variance unless told otherwise -- so TRUE is the correct value for a default QtlDataset fit and the old FALSE was wrong. Verified the only change: with that one column neutralised, old vs new are all.equal at 1e-6.

(1) The joint engine now supplies allele frequencies to postprocessFinemappingFits() (it passed af only on the univariate/RSS paths), so top_loci$af is populated for mvsusie/fsusie rows instead of all-NA. Re-baselined 2026-10-13: genomicRegion() is now the ANALYSIS WINDOW, stored at construction, rather than the derived span of the variants that survived QC -- the span is still available as range(x). The collection therefore carries a `region` mcols column and the per-row grange_start/grange_end are populated (previously NA on every path, because no caller passed `region` to postprocessFinemappingFits). Verified the ONLY change: with the `region` column and grange_* dropped, old vs new are all.equal at 1e-6. Re-baselined 2026-10-15 for the pecotmr published-output rework (resultWriters.R: writeFineMappingBed/writeSumStatsVcf -> exportToBed/exportToVcf). Verified no existing value moved: over the columns both versions carry and that were populated before, old vs new are all.equal at 1e-6. Adds the dataSource / standardized / z_supplied provenance columns. Re-baselined 2026-10-16 against the installed pecotmr 0.9.3: `standardized` is FALSE -> TRUE. It is DERIVED, not declared -- .fmRecordProvenance() reads .qtlScaleResiduals(), and residualizedGenotypes() scales each genotype column to unit variance unless told otherwise -- so TRUE is the correct value for a default QtlDataset fit and the old FALSE was wrong. Verified the only change: with that one column neutralised, old vs new are all.equal at 1e-6. Also drops the per-variant `conditional_effect` column, deliberately removed in 0.9.3 as redundant: it was exactly posterior_mean / pip, confirmed against the old fixture (ratio 1..1 over all 400 variants).
